# Incident Report: Malware Infection on DESKTOP-KKITB6Q

**Evidence source:** `2021-09-10-traffic-analysis-exercise.pcap` (9,221 frames, ~77 min capture)
**Analysis method:** tshark protocol/statistics analysis, DHCP/NBNS/Kerberos host identification, HTTP object export + hashing, TLS/certificate inspection. No internet lookups performed (per instructions); no AV/YARA/hash-reputation check was run, so malware family attribution below is **behavioral, not signature-confirmed**.

## 1. Infected host

| Attribute | Value |
|---|---|
| IPv4 address | **10.9.10.102** |
| MAC address | **00:4f:49:b1:e8:c3** |
| Windows hostname | **DESKTOP-KKITB6Q** |
| Windows domain | ANGRYPOUTINE.COM |
| Logged-in user | **hobart.gunnarsson** (confirmed via Kerberos AS-REQ/TGS-REQ exchanges with the DC at 10.9.10.9, `ANGRYPOUTINE-DC`) |

## 2. Malware family

No YARA/AV/hash-reputation lookup was possible (no internet access). Attribution is therefore **behavioral only**:

- Frame 1189 (tcp.stream 50, t=139.7s): HTTP GET to `simpsonsavingss.com` using a spoofed legacy User-Agent (`Mozilla/4.0 (compatible; MSIE 7.0; ... Trident/7.0 ...)`) — a signature of malware downloader traffic, not a real browser.
- Server returned a 284,816-byte `application/octet-stream` file (`Content-Disposition: attachment; filename="date6"`), which is a **PE32+ DLL** with only `DllRegisterServer`/`DllUnregisterServer` exports and a minimal import table (`VirtualAlloc`, `VirtualFree`, `CreateThread`, `WaitForMultipleObjects`, `GetProcAddress`) plus garbled/obfuscated internal strings — the classic shape of a shellcode-loading stager DLL (designed to be run via `regsvr32`/`rundll32`).
- ~4.3 seconds after the download completed, the host opened a fresh TLS session (tcp.stream 51, t=144.0s) to a different IP on port 443, presented **no SNI**, and negotiated a **self-signed certificate** (CN `londonareloeli.uk`, O="LL EST", OU="UK System", L/ST="London", C=GB — issuer identical to subject). This single 4.5-second burst pulled down ~303 KB from the server to the host — consistent with the stager fetching a second-stage payload/config over an encrypted, non-legitimate channel.

This chain (fake-browser-UA HTTP downloader → minimal-import DLL stager → immediate TLS callout to a self-signed "UK"-themed certificate) matches the well-documented **downloader-delivers-Cobalt-Strike/BazarLoader-style loader** pattern seen in 2021 malspam campaigns (e.g., Hancitor-class delivery chains). I cannot name a specific family with certainty without signature/hash-intel confirmation; treat the label as a working hypothesis, not a confirmed verdict.

## 3. Indicators of Compromise (all observed directly in the capture)

**Malicious domain / distribution site:**
- `simpsonsavingss.com` → resolved to **194.62.42.206**

**Malicious URL (stager download):**
- `http://simpsonsavingss.com/bmdff/BhoHsCtZ/MLdmpfjaX/5uFG3Dz7yt/date1?BNLv65=pAAS`

**Transferred file:**
- Server-declared filename: `date6` (requested path segment `date1`)
- Size: 284,816 bytes
- Type: PE32+ DLL (x86-64)
- **SHA256: `eed363fc4af7a9070d69340592dcab7c78db4f90710357de29e3b624aa957cf8`**

**Command-and-control endpoint:**
- **167.172.37.9:443** (TLS, self-signed cert CN `londonareloeli.uk`, no SNI sent, single ~4.5s/303 KB session at capture time t=144s)

**Suspicious/unresolved query of note (not confirmed malicious, worth flagging):**
- `myexternalip.com` — queried by the victim host; commonly used by malware/loaders to fingerprint the public IP, but no follow-on traffic to it was captured, so it is listed as a lower-confidence indicator only.

## Summary
DESKTOP-KKITB6Q (10.9.10.102, MAC 00:4f:49:b1:e8:c3), logged in as domain user hobart.gunnarsson (ANGRYPOUTINE.COM), retrieved a malicious DLL stager (SHA256 `eed363fc4af7a9070d69340592dcab7c78db4f90710357de29e3b658a957cf8`... see hash above) from `simpsonsavingss.com` (194.62.42.206) using spoofed browser headers, then immediately beaconed out over TLS to `167.172.37.9:443` using a self-signed certificate impersonating a UK entity, pulling down a further ~303 KB payload. Attribution to a specific named malware family is behavioral/circumstantial given no signature-check capability was available in this analysis.
